title: DINOv3 Beats Specialized Detectors: A Simple Foundation Model Baseline for Image Forensics
mechanism: Frozen DINOv3 ViT backbone with LoRA plus a lightweight convolutional decoder for pixel-level localisation of small manipulated regions. LoRA beats full fine-tuning, which is unstable on scarce data.
adaptation: Repeat 1-channel EL to 3 channels; 512 or 1024 px input; add a stride-2 CNN stem skip into the conv decoder so 1-2 px cracks survive the patch-16 grid; 24-class CE plus Dice on crack and inactive as in the house recipe. DINOv3 is gated (user OK needed); fallback DINOv2-L or C-RADIOv4.
min_experiment: Arm: frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 + LoRA r16 + conv decoder + stem skip, 1024 px, 20k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house PF 5-seed. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test crack relF1@2 and IoU. Kill: after 2 seeds, E1 relF1@2 below PF + 0.02 and test relF1@2 below PF.
evidence: R: +17.0 average pixel F1 over previous SOTA on 4 benchmarks (CAT-Net protocol) with 9.1M trainable params on frozen ViT-L; data-scarce MVSS protocol F1 0.774 vs 0.530; LoRA > full FT at all backbone scales. E: our house fine-tune erases the encoder and PF keeps it, the same pattern.
prior_overlap: Partial. BRIEF section 5 ran frozen linear probes of small VFMs and one DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T PF screen; ViT-L with LoRA and a conv decoder is listed as open. D24 covers VFM PEFT in general but not this paper.
